mechanism_narrative: Because WORKPLACES has stayed depressed while RESIDENTIAL remains elevated, weekday shopping is still being substituted by at-home routines. If this labor-activity pattern persists, RETAIL_REC will drift lower over the next four weeks relative to the prior four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days while WORKPLACES does not recover and RESIDENTIAL does not decline from the current elevated level.

mechanism_narrative: A recent improvement in TRANSIT usage indicates more external trips and higher exposure to commercial areas. If TRANSIT continues to stabilize or rise for two more weeks, RETAIL_REC will increase within the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT stops falling and posts a weekly increase from t-0w
failure_condition: TRANSIT improves for at least two consecutive weeks but RETAIL_REC does not move above its current level within 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: If both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES weaken together, the city is shifting into a lower-attendance mobility regime that suppresses discretionary shopping trips. The combined decline should push RETAIL_REC down over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES fall below their t-1w levels in the same week
failure_condition: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both weaken but RETAIL_REC is not lower on average over the next 28 days than over the prior 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: An upswing in PARKS mobility signals warmer-weather discretionary out-of-home activity that spills into nearby retail visits. When PARKS rises above its recent range, RETAIL_REC should increase over the following four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS exceeds its t-3w mean by at least 5 points
failure_condition: PARKS rises materially above its recent level but RETAIL_REC remains flat or falls over the next 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: Rising GROCERY_PHARM mobility signals more errand-based trips and localized activity density, which can spill into adjacent retail outings. If grocery-and-pharmacy mobility stays near zero or turns positive, RETAIL_REC should improve within one week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM crosses from negative to nonnegative week-on-week
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM turns nonnegative but RETAIL_REC does not increase in the following week.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL stays high while TRANSIT stays deeply negative, people are substituting home-centered routines for shopping trips. That combination should keep RETAIL_REC below its recent average over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL remains above +15 while TRANSIT remains below -30 for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: The residential-high/transit-low pattern persists for two weeks and RETAIL_REC still rises above its last-four-week mean.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in WORKPLACES is a leading indicator of broader daytime circulation and lunch-and-after-work shopping. If WORKPLACES moves up from the current depressed level, RETAIL_REC should rise over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises by at least 3 points from its current weekly mean
failure_condition: WORKPLACES rises by 3 or more points but RETAIL_REC does not improve over the following 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in TRANSIT and GROCERY_PHARM implies more multi-purpose trips and stronger short-trip chaining, which should lift discretionary retail visits quickly. The effect should appear within two weeks and fail if either series does not improve together.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and GROCERY_PHARM both move upward from their current weekly means
failure_condition: TRANSIT and GROCERY_PHARM both rise but RETAIL_REC does not increase within 14 days.
